entries.reason: a regressor fitted by least squares with a ridge penalty, over the release's own BLAS and LAPACK. The L1 penalty it also declares is REFUSED with an error rather than ignored, and the iteration schedule it also declares is carried and not used because the direct solve returns the minimum an iterative scheme converges to
entries.effect: the fitted model, or LinearModelError.l1PenaltyNotImplemented when an L1 penalty was asked for

entries.reason: the fitted coefficients, the intercept first, and a prediction that is the intercept and the dot product of the features and the weights. A prediction of a different width is refused by name: a dot product of two vectors of different lengths is a truncation or an out-of-bounds read, and a caller who got a number back would believe a prediction about a model they do not hold
entries.effect: the prediction, or LinearModelError.shapeMismatch naming both widths
entries.source: the SDK 26.2 CreateMLComponents.swiftinterface; the refusals are this port's and the reasons are in the facts

entries.reason: a classifier fitted one class at a time, one-against-the-rest, each by the same ridge fit, with the probabilities from the logistic link over the class scores
entries.effect: the fitted model, or LinearModelError.l1PenaltyNotImplemented when an L1 penalty was asked for

entries.reason: the per-class coefficients in class-major order, an intercept per class and then one weight per class per feature, and the class distribution a prediction answers. featureCount is (coefficients.count - 1) / classes, because a two-class model over one feature has three coefficients and calling that two features refuses every prediction of it
entries.effect: the label, and the probability of every class

something that takes a feature vector and answers a number, for one input or a sequence of them. A classifier is NOT a regressor: its output is a distribution and not a number, and a protocol that covered both would say the wrong thing about half of them

entries.reason: a feature vector and the target that goes with it, as a NAMED type rather than a tuple: the two fitted(to:) overloads are told apart by their argument type, and a tuple is not one - with a tuple the compiler resolves the closure before it knows which overload is meant
a prediction and the target it was made against, which is what an evaluation reads

NOT APPLE'S SURFACE AND NOT IN THE LEDGER. The SDK 26.2 CreateMLComponents declares no `LinearModelError`; its public error enums are OptimizationError, EstimatorEncodingError, DatasetError and ModelUpdateError, and the surface has 0 rows for it. It is the port's own error for the linear models - a width the model was not fitted for, too few rows, a design with no answer, an L1 penalty this build does not fit - and it lives in the package's own registry so that nothing reads it as a row of Apple's
entries.effect: the reason, in the framework's own words
